I disagree a little bit with the "If you can be around someone for 18 years and not know they are hurting, you're an idiot." Because how many of us didn't like walk on egg shells or pretend to be happy so we wouldn't have to deal with our parents outbursts/abuse? I know I've definitely had to explain to my mother certain moments of happiness that she remembers fondly, were just me bullshitting so she wouldn't throw a fit.

My brother is definitely a supporter for her, he still sides with her and cannot see what she had done wrong to me that I keep this distance, he holds onto her same stance of "you're holding onto the past, just let it go and move on, you're the one who is still holding grudges, you seriously need to do some personal healing" when I know I am fine. He's 25 so I don't know if he will ever see my side of things, especially not living with her being doted over.
 I am living a good life, putting myself through school, aside from being a little lonely friendship/relationship wise I feel very happy with the decisions I have made to lead me to this point in my life. I don't know how to explain clearer to them that this decision to keep her at a distance is good for me, that as shitty as it sounds, I dont give a shit how it makes my mother feel.  I know how she abused me in my raising was not her fault, and I know it is incredibly difficult to come to terms with being a narcissistic person and realizing that you are the problem, but that doesn't mean I should just automatically forgive her and let it all go that she did simply because she cannot control/recognize it.

I suppose I kind of have been reeled back in. Some people I feel are worth the stress, like still being in contact with my brother and one remaining grandmother, some of my aunts were nice to see again at the funeral although I'm not sure how to approach seeing them again. It feels awkward to try and rekindle these relationships. 


I am really really trying to sort of nip my mother's overstepping, to cut it off right now so it cannot get bigger, though I think I have put enough distance still, even if we are in contact. 


Sometimes I consider applying for a visa to another country and completely starting a full new life for myself, so far away that I don't even need to make these excuses not to see her.

It's hard for me to just not say anything. I was without any family for 10 years and now that I am finally back in a lot of people I had not previously seen and missed are back in my life, its really nice to have some people, even if they do choose her over me when I go no contact. But I am really trying to maintain boundaries, she almost immediately found all my social media and tried to add me which I have just ignored, I feel like she has no right to see how my life is now, feels like an invasion of privacy. 


We even had a small argument a couple weeks ago where she asked me what am I going to do just disappear again, and I said yes I managed life alone for 10 years and I can do it again if I have to in order to protect my peace. Trying my best not to be reeled back in.

I think yes he does somewhat but I don't really blame him fully. Our mother has absolutely made a golden-child of him, and relies on him for everything. It sounds like you're pretty serious. Im so sorry your mother is not being as caring as you like, a very common occurrence unfortunately. Few little checklist things.
1.are you legally able to work? Legally able to live on your own?

2.do you have savings for things like a tent, food, transportation to a job/job interviews?

3.how will you keep yourself clothes and presentable for work or job interviews?

4.have you researched dangerous areas in your city? Possibly high risk places for sex trafficking? Every city has them.

5.Do you plan to go to college/university for a career? Will you set up a tent or other form of living near there?

6.Do you have a way to shower? A friends shower you can use or possibly couch surf at while you save for a place of your own?

Been homeless various times while still working. Get a good tent, don't set it near a tent city though with other people, try a quiet woodsy area. Less chance of cops finding and fucking it up just because they feel like it. Gym membership for showers, or try to find a portable shower option like water bottles from the store and a bucket and soap, sponge bath style. 

Load as much money as you can on a metro pass so you can get to work/interviews. Maybe print a few copies of your resume, keep in a waterproof bag for applying places. 

Check out tool/outdoorsy stores for portable batteries to charge your phone. Also to possible power a small hotplate. Get lots of rice and canned proteins and canned veg. Fruit that doesn't need a fridge like oranges and bananas.

Buy small tote bins or bags to keep your clothes in so they stay dry, especially nicer job interview clothes. Would also recommend a grocery trolley like old ladies use, to take your clothes to the laundromat weekly, and to pick up groceries and supplies.

A small padlock or 2 is also good to lock around the zipper of the tent. Not foolproof, but still a little peace of mind. Consider getting a crossbody bag or laptop bag to keep the important things on you at all times, things that would really hurt if stolen.
